newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds off lows despite U.S. anchor.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds off lows despite U.S. anchor.

text.p: *Australian bond prices ended above the day's opening lows as they attempted to shake off the shackles of a fragile U.S. bond market once it saw another set of favourable data.
*A modest rise in imports kept rate cut hopes alive.

Australian bond yields ended only modestly higher as the market rowed back from an initial U.S. led spike after it saw more favourable data to suggest that a local rate cut remains on the cards before year end.

"The Aussie bond market believes that the economy is soft out there. It possibly wants to see the next inflation number, but it looks like it has a bit further to rally," said David de Garis, treasury economist at ANZ Banking.
Today's data showed a softer than expected 1.0 percent rise in August merchandise imports after three months of falls.

Economists median forecasts had centred on a 2.2 percent increase, and this modest imports rise, which included a A$93 million aircraft, is expected to keep the current account deficit fairly contained at A$1.2 to A$1.5 billion.

"Recent news on input prices, the expectation of a good CPI in October and tighter fiscal policy, together with today's weak import numbers make bonds "a buy"," said Hans Kunnen, chief economist at State Bank New South Wales.
A policy easing at the November RBA board meeting is seen as the most opportune time, and after the October 23 third quarter inflation report and August wages data the next day.

The December 90-day bill futuers contract is already pricing in a 25 basis point cut in current 7.0 percent official interest rates, despite easing five basis points to 93.27 after fears flared up again over a tightening in U.S. policy.

Comments by a Federal Reserve official that the Fed appears to be centring on around a 25 basis point hike in September sent the U.S. market down sharply on Tuesday and dragged the local 10-year bond yield back above 8.0 percent at one stage.
However, follow-through demand after Tuesday's aggressively bid T-bond tender and the soft data helped yields remain close to this week's three-week lows.

The local market outperformed the U.S. with spreads narrowing again, although the market is finding resistance at around 110/111 basis points, the lowest level in over two years. New Zealand debt finally rebounded after lagging the dollar bloc in recent days, helped by a soaring N.Z. dollar.
